title: The Qur'an as first source
hookLine: every school begins with the Qur'an

lines: A COMMAND, A LINK, A REASON.
cards: "O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)." That's a verse of law, in Pickthall's translation of the Qur'an.
Listen to what's packed into one breath. Who it speaks to. A command.
A link to people who came before. And a reason. When the schools of law sit down to work out a ruling, this is where they start: with the book, read slowly, phrase by phrase.
Today: the Qur'an as first source.

teach.b: First, why first. Muslims hold the Qur'an to be the speech of Allah, and the schools of law, Sunni and Shia, begin their reasoning there. A well-known report puts it as a scene.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is sending Mu'adh ibn Jabal to Yemen as a judge, and asks how he'll judge. By the Book of Allah, Mu'adh says. And if it isn't there?
By the sunnah. And if it isn't there? By my own careful reasoning.
Hadith critics have graded that report differently, exactly what the last block taught us to notice. But the order it describes is the order the schools teach. Second, where the law sits.
The verses of law aren't gathered into one chapter.
They sit among stories, prayers, promises and warnings, so a jurist reads the whole book to find them. Third, the reasons.

Like the fasting verse, a ruling often comes with its purpose attached: that ye may ward off evil. Jurists pay close attention to those purposes, and later in this block that attention becomes a method of its own.
Fourth, the limits of a single source.
The Qur'an commands prayer again and again, but doesn't spell out every movement of it. For that, scholars turn to the second source, tomorrow.

And since today ends a week, look back along it: careful with the weak, forty to carry, explained for us, with a teacher, the chain held, the path and the map. Each was about how carefully a tradition handles its sources.

how: In Islamic law, scholars of the Sunni and Shia schools begin with the Qur'an when working out a ruling, reading its verses of law closely along with their context and purposes.

games.q: what does “the qur'an as first source” mean?
o: the schools begin their reasoning from the Qur'an, read closely
the oldest Qur'an manuscript, kept as the model copy

games.q: you're Mu'adh, about to leave for Yemen as a judge. the Prophet asks how you will judge. what do you say?
o: by the Book of Allah, then the sunnah, then my own careful reasoning.
by whatever the local custom is.
games.why: in the report, Mu'adh names the book first, then the sunnah, then his own striving, and the Prophet approves.

practice: Read the fasting verse in its pieces, with a breath between each: O ye who believe, who it speaks to; fasting is prescribed for you, the command; even as it was prescribed for those before you, a link to others; that ye may ward off evil, the reason.
Then rest on the last piece and let one question sit with you: what is this command for?
